title: CASE/UCO SDK Extension Manifest
description: Metadata schema for extension ontologies that extend the CASE/UCO ecosystem. Each extension directory under extensions/ must contain a manifest.json conforming to this schema.

name.description: Short identifier used as the extension directory name and package suffix (e.g., 'cac', 'aeo').

display_name.description: Human-readable name for documentation and CLI output.

version.description: Version of the upstream ontology this extension tracks. Extension binding packages use this as their package version.

upstream_repo.description: URL of the upstream ontology repository.

upstream_ref.description: Git tag, branch, or commit SHA the submodule is pinned to.

license.description: SPDX license identifier for the extension ontology.

namespaces.description: Map of prefix -> namespace URI for all namespaces defined by this extension. Used by the generator for module classification instead of heuristic detection.

ontology_submodule.description: Relative path from the extension directory to the git submodule root (typically 'ontology').

owl_files.description: Relative paths (from extension directory) to OWL definition files to parse. Order matters: load spine/core files before domain modules.

shacl_files.description: Relative paths to SHACL shapes files. May be empty if SHACL is embedded in OWL files (as with AEO).

bridge_files.description: Relative paths to bridge/alignment modules (e.g., UCO bridge, CASE bridge, gUFO bridge). Loaded for validation but not for class generation.

exemplar_files.description: Relative paths to example instance data files (A-Box). Used for validation testing only.

invalid_exemplar_files.description: Relative paths to expected-invalid negative fixtures (A-Box) that must fail SHACL validation. Used to test that the extension's shapes actually reject nonconformant data, rather than passing everything.

status.description: Lifecycle status, per mcp_server/knowledge_lifecycle.py. Absent means operational (the bundled extensions predate the lifecycle). Candidate extensions are invisible to routing but can be loaded explicitly by name for validation.

file.description: Relative path to a SPARQL query file.

against.description: Relative path to the graph the query is run against.

expect.description: Whether the query must return rows. Defaults to nonempty in the promotion gate.

promotion.description: Provenance recorded by `make promote-extension`: reviewer, timestamp, git commit, and deployment profile at the time of promotion.

deprecation.description: Provenance recorded by `make deprecate-extension`: reason and timestamp.

class_registry.description: Whether the code generator adds this extension's classes to the generated per-language class registries and to ONTOLOGY_REFERENCE.md / MAPPING_GUIDE.md. Set false for large generated catalogs whose classes carry no properties of their own (e.g. the MITRE ATT&CK and ATLAS technique catalogs); they are listed by pointer instead and discovered through their MCP tools. Validation still loads the extension's files.

distribution.description: Where the extension may be distributed. A private extension is never loaded by the code generator, so the generated class registries and reference docs are identical with or without it, and scripts/public_export.py leaves its directory out of the public tree. Validation, the extension's own _registry.json and MCP discovery via CASE_UCO_EXTENSIONS work as for any other extension.

depends_on.description: Names of other extensions whose terms this extension's exemplars or shapes reuse; expanded by resolve_extension_dependencies().

provenance.description: Where the extension's definitions came from when they mirror or forward-implement terms authored elsewhere (e.g. an upstream pull request). Free-form; used for attribution and for recording a retirement condition.

uco_compat.description: List of UCO/CASE versions this extension is known to be compatible with (e.g., ['1.4.0', '1.5.0']).

upper_ontology.description: Which upper/foundational ontology this extension directly depends on, if any. Use an array when an extension bridges to more than one. Machine-readable by design: put any explanation in upper_ontology_notes rather than here.

upper_ontology_notes.description: Prose describing how the upper-ontology alignment is realised — which bridge file carries it, which classes are mapped, and anything delegated by reference instead of modelled.

cdo_shapes_compatibility.description: Compatibility status of each CDO Shapes profile with this extension. 'included' means the extension already provides this alignment. 'not_recommended' means loading both may produce conflicting axioms. Machine-readable by design: put any explanation in cdo_shapes_notes.

cdo_shapes_notes.description: Optional per-profile prose explaining a cdo_shapes_compatibility verdict. Keys should match those used there.
